pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes that workflow emails are still sent for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. The fix of PR #6991 was wrong and didn't work as expected. 

The SendGrid endpoint `DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/${referenceId}` was not used correctly. This endpoint deletes a cancelled scheduled email from `scheduled_sends` by removing the 'cancel' status (so email will again be scheduled). 

The reason why cancelling our scheduled emails stopped working is that all cancerlled emails are saved in `scheduled_sends` until the scheduled date but the max. of pending cancellations is 100. Once we reached 100 pending cancellations, new cancellations failed and emails were still sent out. 

The solution implemented in this PR: 
- A new field `cancelled` is added to the `workflowReminder` model
- Once an already scheduled email is cancelled, the field is set to true (nothing else is done at this point in time)
- The CRON job `scheduleEmailReminders` is responsible for the final cancellation of the scheduled email (runs every 15 mins)
  - cancels all scheduled emails that are cancelled and that have their scheduled date within the next hour

Fixes #7225

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Chore (refactoring code, technical debt, workflow improvements)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update
pr.title: Fixes that workflow reminders of cancelled and rescheduled bookings are still sent

raw_findings.body: The HTTP response can be returned (req.statusCode = 200) before the reminder cancellation/cleanup (SendGrid cancel or DB `cancelled` flag update) completes; if the runtime tears down the function immediately after responding, the reminder is neither marked cancelled nor deleted, so the scheduled workflow email/SMS can still be sent for the cancelled booking — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of completion guarantee causes silently skipped/lost reminder cancellation under early process termination.
raw_findings.impact: The HTTP response can be returned (req.statusCode = 200) before the reminder cancellation/cleanup (SendGrid cancel or DB `cancelled` flag update) completes; if the runtime tears down the function immediately after responding, the reminder is neither marked cancelled nor deleted, so the scheduled workflow email/SMS can still be sent for the cancelled booking — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix.
raw_findings.root_cause: Explicit awaited deletion of WorkflowReminder rows (remindersToDelete) was removed and replaced with unawaited fire-and-forget calls whose internal DB writes are no longer guaranteed to complete before the handler returns.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Collect the promises returned by deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and include them in prismaPromises (or a separate await Promise.all) before responding to the request.
raw_findings.title: Workflow reminder cleanup on booking cancellation no longer awaited before response
raw_findings.trigger: A booking with scheduled email/SMS workflow reminders is cancelled; deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside a forEach without await, and the previous explicit awaited workflowReminder.deleteMany() calls for these reminders were removed from prismaPromises.

raw_findings.body: The mutation can resolve before reminder cancellation/DB update completes; if the process exits or is recycled right after the response, the old booking's workflow reminders remain scheduled and may still be sent even though the booking was rescheduled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of completion guarantee for reminder cancellation during reschedule.
raw_findings.impact: The mutation can resolve before reminder cancellation/DB update completes; if the process exits or is recycled right after the response, the old booking's workflow reminders remain scheduled and may still be sent even though the booking was rescheduled.
raw_findings.root_cause: Removal of the explicit awaited remindersToDelete/Promise.all cleanup, relying instead on unawaited async helper calls.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Have deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder return their promises, collect them into an array, and await Promise.all on that array before completing the mutation.
raw_findings.title: Workflow reminder cleanup on booking reschedule no longer awaited
raw_findings.trigger: requestReschedule mutation is called for a booking that has workflow reminders; deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are invoked in a forEach without await and the array/await that previously guaranteed workflowReminder cleanup completion is deleted.

raw_findings.body: The mutation can complete before the corresponding WorkflowReminder rows are marked cancelled/deleted, risking reminders for now-inactive event types remaining scheduled and being sent later.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of completion guarantee for reminder cancellation during workflow update.
raw_findings.impact: The mutation can complete before the corresponding WorkflowReminder rows are marked cancelled/deleted, risking reminders for now-inactive event types remaining scheduled and being sent later.
raw_findings.root_cause: Removal of the explicit awaited deleteReminderPromise array/Promise.all guarding reminder row cleanup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Collect promises from deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder and await them (e.g. via Promise.all) before the mutation returns.
raw_findings.title: Workflow reminder cleanup for disabled event types no longer awaited
raw_findings.trigger: Editing a workflow that disables event types with existing scheduled reminders triggers remindersToDelete.flat().forEach, calling deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await; the previous awaited deleteReminderPromise/Promise.all cleanup was removed.

raw_findings.body: The WorkflowReminder row for the rescheduled booking is never deleted or marked cancelled — it remains in the database with scheduled: true and stale referenceId, contributing to data bloat and inconsistent state until its scheduledDate eventually passes and the periodic deleteMany cleans it up.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale WorkflowReminder rows accumulate for rescheduled bookings, silently bypassing cleanup.
raw_findings.impact: The WorkflowReminder row for the rescheduled booking is never deleted or marked cancelled — it remains in the database with scheduled: true and stale referenceId, contributing to data bloat and inconsistent state until its scheduledDate eventually passes and the periodic deleteMany cleans it up.
raw_findings.root_cause: The immediateDelete branch only performs the external cancellation call and returns, omitting the corresponding Prisma delete/update that other branches perform.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In the immediateDelete branch, delete (or mark cancelled) the WorkflowReminder row after successfully cancelling with SendGrid, instead of returning without touching the database.
raw_findings.title: Immediate-delete path leaves orphaned WorkflowReminder rows after reschedule
raw_findings.trigger: handleNewBooking.ts calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) for the previous booking's workflow reminders during a reschedule; the old booking row is kept (marked cancelled/rescheduled) rather than deleted, so no cascade removes the reminder.

raw_findings.body: The loop aborts on the first exception; all subsequent reminders in that CRON run are neither cancelled nor deleted, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose reminders are due imminently may still be sent by SendGrid before the next CRON run 15 minutes later retries them.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Batch cancellation processing halts on first error, delaying cancellation of other due reminders.
raw_findings.impact: The loop aborts on the first exception; all subsequent reminders in that CRON run are neither cancelled nor deleted, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose reminders are due imminently may still be sent by SendGrid before the next CRON run 15 minutes later retries them.
raw_findings.root_cause: A single try/catch wraps the entire for-loop, causing one failure to short-circuit processing of all remaining items.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each iteration's cancel+delete logic in its own try/catch so a failure for one reminder does not prevent processing of the remaining reminders in the batch.
raw_findings.title: Single failed SendGrid cancel call aborts cancellation of all remaining due reminders in the batch
raw_findings.trigger: The SendGrid /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel request throws for one reminder in remindersToCancel (e.g., transient network/API error) while other reminders in the same batch are due to be sent within the next hour.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Ambiguous tri-state boolean semantics for a field intended to be binary.
raw_findings.impact: Inconsistent representation of the 'not cancelled' state (NULL vs false) makes queries/comparisons (e.g. `cancelled: true` filters) rely on NULL being falsy, and complicates future non-nullable refactors or strict equality checks against the field.
raw_findings.root_cause: New boolean column added as nullable without a default value, unlike the existing `scheduled` field in the same model.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the field as `cancelled Boolean @default(false)` to match the non-nullable `scheduled Boolean` field convention used elsewhere in this model.

raw_findings.trigger: Any existing WorkflowReminder row created before this migration, or any code path that doesn't explicitly set cancelled, will have cancelled = NULL rather than false.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in this critical cancellation path (e.g., the batch-abort issue on partial failure, or query filter mistakes) could go undetected, silently reintroducing the bug this PR fixes.

raw_findings.root_cause: New critical cancellation logic was added without accompanying test coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit/integration test for scheduleEmailReminders that verifies reminders marked cancelled and due within the next hour are cancelled via SendGrid and removed from the database, including a case where one cancellation fails.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage added for new deferred email-reminder cancellation CRON logic
raw_findings.trigger: This new deferred cancellation block (querying `cancelled: true` reminders due within an hour, issuing SendGrid cancel, then deleting) is the core mechanism the PR relies on to actually prevent emails from being sent, but no test exercises it.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: The cited line 397 'await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)' is on the LEFT side (old code being removed). The patch intentionally removes this because the new architecture uses deferred cancellation via the cancelled flag. The new deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder mark reminders cancelled, and the CRON job handles actual cancellation. This is design intent, not a bug.

validated_findings.body: The WorkflowReminder row for the rescheduled booking is never deleted or marked cancelled — it remains in the database with scheduled: true and stale referenceId, contributing to data bloat and inconsistent state until its scheduledDate eventually passes and the periodic deleteMany cleans it up.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale WorkflowReminder rows accumulate for rescheduled bookings, silently bypassing cleanup.
validated_findings.impact: The WorkflowReminder row for the rescheduled booking is never deleted or marked cancelled — it remains in the database with scheduled: true and stale referenceId, contributing to data bloat and inconsistent state until its scheduledDate eventually passes and the periodic deleteMany cleans it up.
validated_findings.root_cause: The immediateDelete branch only performs the external cancellation call and returns, omitting the corresponding Prisma delete/update that other branches perform.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: In the immediateDelete branch, delete (or mark cancelled) the WorkflowReminder row after successfully cancelling with SendGrid, instead of returning without touching the database.
validated_findings.title: Immediate-delete path leaves orphaned WorkflowReminder rows after reschedule
validated_findings.trigger: handleNewBooking.ts calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) for the previous booking's workflow reminders during a reschedule; the old booking row is kept (marked cancelled/rescheduled) rather than deleted, so no cascade removes the reminder.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at emailReminderManager.ts lines 213-223 shows the immediateDelete branch calls SendGrid cancel and returns without any database operation. Lines 203-210 show the no-referenceId branch deletes the row, and lines 225-230 show the normal branch updates cancelled:true. But immediateDelete (line 222: return) skips both. handleNewBooking.ts calls with immediateDelete=true for reschedules, leaving orphaned WorkflowReminder rows.

validated_findings.body: The loop aborts on the first exception; all subsequent reminders in that CRON run are neither cancelled nor deleted, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose reminders are due imminently may still be sent by SendGrid before the next CRON run 15 minutes later retries them.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Batch cancellation processing halts on first error, delaying cancellation of other due reminders.
validated_findings.impact: The loop aborts on the first exception; all subsequent reminders in that CRON run are neither cancelled nor deleted, so cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose reminders are due imminently may still be sent by SendGrid before the next CRON run 15 minutes later retries them.
validated_findings.root_cause: A single try/catch wraps the entire for-loop, causing one failure to short-circuit processing of all remaining items.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each iteration's cancel+delete logic in its own try/catch so a failure for one reminder does not prevent processing of the remaining reminders in the batch.
validated_findings.title: Single failed SendGrid cancel call aborts cancellation of all remaining due reminders in the batch
validated_findings.trigger: The SendGrid /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel request throws for one reminder in remindersToCancel (e.g., transient network/API error) while other reminders in the same batch are due to be sent within the next hour.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 53-70 shows a single try/catch wrapping the entire for-loop. If client.request throws at line 57 for one reminder, the catch at line 72 logs and exits, skipping all subsequent reminders. Each iteration should have its own try/catch to ensure one failure doesn't abort processing of remaining due reminders.

validated_findings.body: Inconsistent representation of the 'not cancelled' state (NULL vs false) makes queries/comparisons (e.g. `cancelled: true` filters) rely on NULL being falsy, and complicates future non-nullable refactors or strict equality checks against the field.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Ambiguous tri-state boolean semantics for a field intended to be binary.
validated_findings.impact: Inconsistent representation of the 'not cancelled' state (NULL vs false) makes queries/comparisons (e.g. `cancelled: true` filters) rely on NULL being falsy, and complicates future non-nullable refactors or strict equality checks against the field.
validated_findings.root_cause: New boolean column added as nullable without a default value, unlike the existing `scheduled` field in the same model.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the field as `cancelled Boolean @default(false)` to match the non-nullable `scheduled Boolean` field convention used elsewhere in this model.
validated_findings.title: New cancelled field is nullable without a default, inconsistent with sibling boolean fields
validated_findings.trigger: Any existing WorkflowReminder row created before this migration, or any code path that doesn't explicitly set cancelled, will have cancelled = NULL rather than false.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at schema.prisma line 644 shows 'cancelled Boolean?' as nullable without default. Line 641 shows 'scheduled Boolean' is non-nullable. This inconsistency means existing rows and new rows without explicit cancelled value will have NULL, creating tri-state semantics (true/false/null) for a binary concept. While functional, it's a data modeling inconsistency that complicates queries.

validated_findings.body: Regressions in this critical cancellation path (e.g., the batch-abort issue on partial failure, or query filter mistakes) could go undetected, silently reintroducing the bug this PR fixes.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Undetected regressions in reminder cancellation logic during future changes.
validated_findings.impact: Regressions in this critical cancellation path (e.g., the batch-abort issue on partial failure, or query filter mistakes) could go undetected, silently reintroducing the bug this PR fixes.
validated_findings.root_cause: New critical cancellation logic was added without accompanying test coverage.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit/integration test for scheduleEmailReminders that verifies reminders marked cancelled and due within the next hour are cancelled via SendGrid and removed from the database, including a case where one cancellation fails.
validated_findings.title: No test coverage added for new deferred email-reminder cancellation CRON logic
validated_findings.trigger: This new deferred cancellation block (querying `cancelled: true` reminders due within an hour, issuing SendGrid cancel, then deleting) is the core mechanism the PR relies on to actually prevent emails from being sent, but no test exercises it.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test_gap category finding about missing test coverage. While potentially valid as a quality concern, it's not a concrete defect introduced by the patch. The absence of tests doesn't constitute a bug in the code itself, and the finding doesn't identify specific incorrect behavior that would be caught by tests.
